ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $AE$ is a straight line, and $O$ is a point on the straight line $AE$. $OB$ is the bisector of $\angle AOC$, and $OD$ is the bisector of $\angle COE$. Given that $\angle AOB=30^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle BOD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $OD$ is the bisector of $\angle COE$,\\
it follows that $\angle COD= \frac{1}{2}\angle COE=60^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle BOD=\angle COD+\angle BOC=60^\circ+30^\circ=\boxed{90^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows AE as a horizontal straight line passing through O, with E on the left side of O and A on the right side. From O, ray OB goes up to the right and lies between OA and OC; ray OC is steeper upward to the right; ray OD goes up to the left and lies between OC and OE. Reasoning: Since OB is the bisector of ∠AOC and ∠AOB = 30°, we have ∠BOC = 30°, so ∠AOC = 60°. Because AE is a straight line, ∠AOE = 180°. Therefore ∠COE = 180° − 60° = 120°. Since OD is the bisector of ∠COE, ∠COD = 120° ÷ 2 = 60°. From the ray order in the image, ∠BOD = ∠BOC + ∠COD = 30° + 60° = 90°.
